text: Many people don't know the difference between the UAE, Abu Dhabi, and Dubai. So, the UAE is a country officially called the United Arab Emirates. Located in the Middle East on the eastern Arabian Peninsula, the country covers about 83,000 square kilometers, which is comparable to Portugal or Austria in size. The UAE is made up of seven federal territories. They're similar to US states, only here they're called Emirates. And that's basically where the name comes from. Each Emirate has its own ruler, a shake, and power is passed down within the ruling family. Essentially like a monarchy, all seven shakes together form the highest governing authority, the Federal Supreme Council, and also elect one of them as President. By tradition, the President is always the shake of Abu Dhabi, the largest Emirate, which covers about 85% of the UAE's territory. Abu Dhabi is both an Emirate and a city with the same name, and the city is the country's capital. Dubai, on the other hand, is a different Emirate, and inside it there is also a city with the same name. Dubai is world famous for its skyline and mega projects, such as the world's tallest skyscraper, the Burj Khalifa, the giant Dubai Mall, almost the size of Vatican City, or even man-made luxury palm-shaped islands.
